windows.title: Ocular for Windows
windows.requirements: Windows 11 24H2 or newer. Intel/AMD 64-bit, or ARM64 with Windows x64 compatibility. S mode and policies blocking installation are not supported.
windows.notice: This personal installer is not publisher-signed. Your browser or Windows may show an unknown-publisher warning. Keep Windows security enabled; a managed computer may require administrator approval.
steps: Download and open OcularSetup.exe. No Python or terminal is needed.
Launch Ocular from your Desktop or Start menu. Startup and tray availability are included.
Press Ctrl+Alt+Shift+O for values, X for text, or A for annotations.
windows.verification: Existing Windows 0.3.2 download preserved. Independent clean-computer installation and hosted automatic-update tests remain outstanding.

chromeos.title: Ocular for ChromeOS
chromeos.requirements: Chrome 116 or newer (API minimum); extensions and Load unpacked must be permitted by device policy. Tested in Chrome 149 on Windows. The HP Chromebox G2 and its policy have not been tested.
chromeos.notice: Free manual edition · manual updates · browser scope. Use Chrome’s extension Developer Mode only. Use a regular ChromeOS user profile. No ChromeOS system Developer Mode, Linux, terminal, Ocular/GitHub account or API key is needed. Organisation policy may prevent installation; do not bypass it.
steps: Download the ZIP and extract it. Opening its temporary mounted folder is not extraction.
Open the extracted Ocular-ChromeOS-0.3.3 folder. Inside it is another folder named Ocular. Move that inner Ocular folder into My files and keep it there.
In Chrome, open Manage Extensions (chrome://extensions) and enable extension Developer Mode.
Choose Load unpacked and select My files > Ocular. Opening that folder should show manifest.json, popup.html and background.mjs.
Pin Ocular in Chrome’s Extensions menu. Try its Calculate, Extract text and Annotate buttons.
Shortcuts while Chrome is focused: Alt+Shift+O for values, Alt+X for text, Alt+A for annotations. Change them through Ocular Settings.
chromeos.verification: Actual Extensions-screen loading, local OCR, captures, copying and same-folder manual update/recovery were checked in an isolated Chrome profile on Windows. Physical Chromebook installation and keyboard checks remain unverified. Capture uses the visible tab; annotations cover browser pages or a labelled captured image. Review OCR before relying on results. Future versions use this same page; save work, replace files in the same folder and Reload the existing extension. See the guide below.
